text:
leo_sales: Starting a Nimbus POC. Customer sees TTFT spikes during interactive flows. Baseline expectation ~150ms, they see 300-900ms. Also asked about Dedicated pricing and a short security checklist. Swarm please.

sam_eng: What model + client? sample request?

leo_sales: model=redwood-7b-compat-v1, prompt ~30 tokens, max_new_tokens=128, streaming=true over websocket, client lib is a custom wrapper. Here's a simplified request payload they send: `{"model":"redwood-7b-compat","prompt":"<user_msg>","max_tokens":128,"stream":true}`

tia_sre: I pulled the runtime trace for their route. Observations: 1) `batcher.queue_delay` often 120-250ms before execution; 2) client sets header `X-Prefer-NoBatch: true` which makes the router dispatch immediately; 3) KV cache warm rate low because prompts include session-specific nonce.

harper_support: They also hit transient 503s during a second of a traffic spike. Logs show `backend_conn.reset` around that window.

sam_eng: Two-pronged approach: (A) client changes: remove `X-Prefer-NoBatch` and reduce per-request unique salts so prefix caching can work; (B) server: adjust route flags to favor batching with small latency target and enable `streaming_chunk_size=64` to send early chunks without forcing one-token microbatches. Example route flags to try: `prefix_cache:true`, `batching.target:6`, `batching.max_latency_ms:40`, `streaming_chunk_bytes:64`.

mina_sec: Quick security concerns: Nimbus needs IP allowlist + KMS-managed keys for the POC. We can do a limited KMS flow for hosted POC and set data_retention=0 for route. I'll prepare the short checklist and a note on minimal controls.

harper_support: I deployed a canary with `prefix_cache=true` and `batching.target=6` for their route. After a small warmup (3 warm requests per worker) median TTFT dropped to ~140ms in our staging run.

tia_sre: Nice. Also recommended client-side concurrency of 3-6 to help aggregation. If they insist on websocket streaming and very low per-user concurrency (1), batching won't be effective.

leo_sales: They want streaming UX but only single connection per user. Can we do a hybrid where we warm and keep a small server-side persistent cache per session?

sam_eng: Yes. Two options: 1) prefix caching + proactive warm on session start (server or client warmup call). 2) lightweight session affinity to reuse warmed kernels. Warmup example (short HTTP warm calls) below.

harper_support: Warmup script (HTTP warm calls):
```bash
for i in 1 2 3 4; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.app/v1/warm
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $POC_KEY"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-compat","prefix":"<stable_prefix>","max_tokens":16}' &
  sleep 0.1
done
wait
```
Run at session start.

sam_eng: For websocket streaming clients we also suggested a tiny preamble message to seed KV: send a 1-2 token preface "\nstream-seed" that is identical across sessions for reuse.

tia_sre: For the 503s, we traced a spike where their proxy retried aggressively (3 retries) causing backend saturation. Recommendation: reduce client retry to exponential backoff and we can put a short grace autoscale window on the route to absorb spikes during POC.

leo_sales: Pricing ask: they want a Dedicated POC for guaranteed consistency during evaluation.

mina_sec: I'll attach the checklist and KMS note in the Nimbus thread.

tia_sre: Dedicated rough estimate: small reserved pool (1xA100-equivalent slot) for the POC at $9k/month for the trial month; include a short autoscale buffer. Finance will confirm.

harper_support: I created a lightweight dashboard share with `first_token_p50/p95`, `batch_size_hist`, and `kv_cache_hit_rate`. Sharing link in the Nimbus ticket.

sam_eng: Follow-ups: ask customer to remove `X-Prefer-NoBatch` if possible, run warmup script 30s before sessions, set client concurrency to 3-5, and avoid per-request unique salts in the prompt. I'll monitor live during their window.

leo_sales: Scheduled interactive session tomorrow 10am PT. Harper/Mina/Tia/Sam please be on standby. I'll send calendar invite to Nimbus. :rocket:
